overview.title: Index: M to O (models to overfitting)
overview.main_topic: Index entries from the 'models' sub-entries to 'overfitting'
overview.central_idea: This page finishes M (scaling up model training, movie-review and multiclass classification, MSE, MultiHeadAttention), covers N (network architectures, neural networks, n-gram, NLP) and covers most of O (object detection, one-hot encoding, optimizers, overfitting).
overview.importance: It points to the classification walkthroughs, multi-device training, object detection and the overfitting discussion.
learning_objectives: Find the multiclass classification, multi-device training and object detection pages
Find where overfitting and its causes are analysed

summary:
Index page printed 616 (PDF 640). Locators are **printed** pages: **add 24** for the PDF page.

**M (end).** *models*: weight regularization 165–166. *model.stateless_call()* 222. *model subclassing* 192. **model training, scaling up with multiple devices** 548–556 (PDF 572–580): distributed training 551–555, multi-GPU training 548–550, TPU training 555. *momentum* 45 (PDF 69). *monitoring with TensorBoard* 212. **movie reviews, classifying** 106–116 (PDF 130–140). *MSE* 116, 134, 360, 602. **multiclass classification** 105, 116–126 (PDF 140–150): Reuters dataset 116, handling labels and loss 124, importance of sufficiently large intermediate layers 125. *MultiHeadAttention layer* 443–447 (PDF 467–471). *multi-hot encoding* 406. *multi-input, multi-output models* 197. *multilabel classification* 105.

**N.** *negative prompt* 532. *Nelder-Mead algorithm* 547. **network architectures** 600–605 (PDF 624–629): convolutional networks 602, densely connected networks 601, RNNs 604, Transformers 603. *neural attention* 603. *neural networks* 7 (PDF 31), with gradient-based optimization 39–50 and mathematical building blocks 16 (PDF 40). *n-gram* 403. *NLP* 381–384, 421 (PDF 405–408). *non-trainable weights* 216.

**O.** **object detection** 309, 329 (PDF 333, 353): RetinaNet 347–349, single-stage vs. two-stage detectors 330–332 (PDF 354–356), training YOLO 342 (PDF 366), COCO 332. *Occam's razor* 165 (PDF 189). *OCR* 329. *one-hot encoding* 118, 406. *ONNX* 185. *on-the-fly adaptation* 580 (PDF 604). *optimizers* 45, 137, 222 (PDF 69). **overfitting** 137–142, 182 (PDF 161–166, 206): ambiguous features 139, noisy training data 138, rare features and spurious correlations 140–142.

concepts.name: overfitting (index entry)
concepts.definition: Indexed at printed 137–142, 182 (PDF 161–166, 206). Sub-entries: noisy training data 138, ambiguous features 139, rare features and spurious correlations 140–142. Recurrent dropout to fight it is on the next page.
concepts.intuition: PDF 161–166 lists the concrete causes of overfitting. PDF 206 belongs to the universal workflow.
concepts.significance: Fighting overfitting is a theme of the whole book.
concepts.misconception: More training epochs do not always help. Past a certain point, validation performance gets worse.

concepts.name: object detection (index entry)
concepts.definition: Indexed at printed 309, 329 (PDF 333, 353). Sub-entries: single- vs. two-stage detectors 330–332, YOLO 336–342, RetinaNet 347–349.
concepts.intuition: The book trains a YOLO-style detector on COCO.
concepts.technical: Related entries: bounding box regression 342, IoU 316, 343, R-CNN 331.
concepts.significance: It is the third main vision task, alongside classification and segmentation.
concepts.misconception: Detection predicts boxes plus classes, not per-pixel masks.

concepts.name: network architectures (index entry)
concepts.definition: Indexed at printed 600–605 (PDF 624–629), the conclusions' review of dense networks, ConvNets, RNNs and Transformers.
concepts.intuition: It is a compact recap of which architecture fits which kind of data.
concepts.technical: Sub-entries: densely connected networks 601, convolutional networks 602, Transformers 603, RNNs 604.
concepts.significance: It works as a revision summary for the whole book.
concepts.misconception: No single architecture is best for every kind of data.
